lines.text: Job asks his friends to listen carefully, bear with him, and then look at him and put their hand over their mouth.
Job asks why the wicked live on, grow old and increase in power, with homes safe from fear.
The children of the wicked skip about singing to the tambourine and lyre, and the wicked go down to Sheol in terror.
Job asks whether the wicked are like grass and chaff swept away by a storm.
Job asks his friends whether they have asked those who travel the roads, and he calls their answers full of falsehood.
